- When sentiment is positive (≥0.2) in recent days, model tends to under-forecast; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% of recent mean or spike magnitude.
- Model consistently over-forecasts after sharp upward spikes in history; apply a “cool-down” correction: reduce forecast by 2–5% for 3–5 days post-spike.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3+ consecutive days below 85–88), model often over-optimistically continues trend; reduce forecast slope by 0.5–1.5% per day.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently fails to capture late-period reversals; add a “tail correction” of -1 to -3% for final 5–7 days if sentiment turns negative or volatility spikes.
- When sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 values, model tends to be overly conservative; increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day to avoid underestimating momentum.
